description:
A Better Way To Manage Your Period
On average, a woman will experience 30 or so years of menstruation in her lifetime, from her first period to menopause. Just one year's supply of disposable pads and tampons can cost between $60 and $120. Doing the math (and lowballing it), that's around $3,600 in a lifetime on a NECCESITY. In addition to that, tampons, panty liners and sanitary napkins, along with their applicator and packaging contribute to around 200,000 tonnes of waste per year. Enter Reusable Menstrual Pads, an alternative that is equally as effective as sanitary pads and tampons.

Why The Hive's Reusable Sanitary Pad for Women?
Our washable pads are free from harmful substances, they are skin friendly, comfortable, sustainable and economical!

What Would I Get?

  • 1x Liner(19cm/7.5 inches)- For light spotting
  • 1x Regular(21cm/8.3 inches)- For regular to medium period flow
  • 1x Ultra(24cm/9.5 inches)- For heavier period flow

How Do I Clean The Pads?
We suggest rinsing the pads thoroughly under running water, then place them in the washing machine, best to use eco-friendly detergent, cold or warm wash recommended. Best to air dry. If using the dryer, LOW TEMPERATURE setting recommended.
Note: Do not use fabric softener or bleach.

How Often Do I Need To Change The Pads?
Naturally, if your flow is heavy, you will have to change pads more frequently. If your flow is lighter, the longer you can take between changes.

How Do I Deal With Pad Changes When I'm On The Go?
You can fold them up into perfect little squares that you can pack away in your purse. You probably will want to carry a waterproof bag with you to keep the used pads, you can wash them at home.

What Is The Shelf Life of The Hive's Sanitary Pad?
Depending on how well you take care of it, the pads can be used for the next 10 years!

There comes a time when we as women start looking for something different, something outside the norm that we know in our hearts will make us feel better about ourselves and improve the planet we live on. We use Lotus liners because they allow us to take care of our bodies in a better way.

HOW DO I CARE FOR MY LINER?

First, we strongly recommend you do not use stain remover on your liners. It is not needed, stain resistance is built right into the fabric composition. Do not bleach your Liners, as it will only fade the colour and unnecessarily breakdown the integrity of the fabric over time. To keep your Liners fresh and stain-free, we recommend soaking after use in cold water and rinsing them out by hand. For stubborn stains on your darkest day, a small amount of hand soap or dish soap will lift the stain in seconds.

Lotus Liners are very resilient and can be washed on a regular cycle with all your other items in both hot or cold water. The material color will not bleed or run, so including them with your other laundry items is absolutely safe. They can be put in the dryer, on a regular cycle and you never have to be concerned with shirking or twisting. Washing on the delicate cycle and hanging them to dry may prolong the life of your liners.

Always unsnap your liners while washing so all the contents are fully removed.

HOW LONG WILL MY LOTUS LINERS LAST?

Lotus Liners are made from a durable long lasting material that has been engineered to last up to five years if cared for by following our washing and drying instructions. We gladly ensure the lifetime warranty of our snaps. If your snap comes off from normal wearing, send the Lotus Liner to us, and we will be happy to replace it, no questions asked.

Buy your Lotus Liners today and join the new generation of women that say no to exposing their bodies to toxic chemicals and yes to preserving the planet for future generations!

Frequently Asked Questions

What’s the difference between Always Ultra Thin and Always Maxi?
Always Ultra Thin pads, in the green package, are super-thin and highly absorbent. Always Maxis, in the blue package, provide the extra feeling of security many women get from using a thicker pad.

How do I put on a pad?
Always pads have adhesive strips to attach securely to your panties. Remove the paper backing and press the sticky side of the pad to your underwear. If your pad also has wings (extra flaps that fold over the sides of your underwear for increased protection), remove the paper backing and wrap the wings around the crotch, pressing firmly to the underside of your panties.

When should I change my pad?
You’ll want to change your pad regularly to stay clean and comfortable; usually every 3–4 hours or more often if your flow is heavy. Remember to match the absorbency of the pad (Regular, Super, or Overnight) to your flow, not your body type.

What’s in the pad?
Always pads have an absorbent core made of processed wood pulp between the plastic top and bottom layers. Always Ultra includes absorbent gelling material in the center of the pad. We use adhesive to hold the pad together.

Is there latex in the pads?
None of our currently marketed Always pads, pantiliners, wipes, or Quickwraps contain any natural rubber latex components. All ingredients in Always are extensively tested for safe use.

There comes a time when we as women start looking for something different, something outside the norm that we know in our hearts will make us feel better about ourselves and improve the planet we live on. We use Lotus liners because they allow us to take care of our bodies in a better way.

HOW DO I CARE FOR MY LINER?

First, we strongly recommend you do not use stain remover on your liners. It is not needed, stain resistance is built right into the fabric composition. Do not bleach your Liners, as it will only fade the colour and unnecessarily breakdown the integrity of the fabric over time. To keep your Liners fresh and stain-free, we recommend soaking after use in cold water and rinsing them out by hand. For stubborn stains on your darkest day, a small amount of hand soap or dish soap will lift the stain in seconds.

Lotus Liners are very resilient and can be washed on a regular cycle with all your other items in both hot or cold water. The material color will not bleed or run, so including them with your other laundry items is absolutely safe. description:
These are so comfortable, unlike regular pads. They are soft and WAY more absorbent than I thought they would be. In fact, I think they are MORE absorbent than normal disposable pads. Normal pads roll up sometimes, they can actually sound crunchy like a diaper, they don't breathe and are hot and sweaty, and they can smell disgusting. These are the opposite! They stay put despite not sticking to your underwear. They actually breathe and there is no "period smell" at all! I am so happy I found these but also so disappointed I never thought to try them years ago!

The medium fit great and are absorbent enough for even a very heavy flow. I went ahead and bought the large, though, so I could have enough to last through my cycle and for the added security for heavy flow overnight.

The washing instructions are to rinse the pad out after use and then just throw them in the wash on gentle. I experimented to make sure they wouldn't dye anything by doing a load with just the pads and a white hand towel and the white towel came out perfectly fine so I think it'll be fine to throw them in with other clothes. I air dried them because, even though the instructions say you can dry on low, I didn't want to risk the nice soft fabric pilling up.

All in all, I strongly recommend these!

UPDATE: I washed on gentle cycle and actually noticed a smell the next time I used them. The next time, I washed them on normal cycle with other laundry because they seemed very well made and sturdy. This worked and no smell. I think that the agitation of other clothes really helps get them clean. I still air-dried.

description:
About Us:
At the core of who we are is the desire to do good, be good and spread good to people, communities, and the environment; Our company was founded on these values and they still guide us today. It is through conscious intention that we offer the cleanest disposal method available, in the cleanest way possible. Our commitment to excellence makes MaskIT tampon disposal bags the premier choice for anyone who wants the best.
MaskIT Sustainability:
We love our planet and do everything we can to reduce our ecological footprint. MaskIT disposal bags are made with plant-based biofilm, derived from the starches of plants and vegetables (mostly potatoes). Our potato-based biofilm does NOT contain any polyethylene or plastic materials whatsoever. In fact, our biofilm can be consumed by microorganisms that naturally live in our soil. Our packaging is made with 100% post-consumer paper and is printed with soy-based ink in a facility that operates on 100% renewable energy.
Why not just use toilet paper?
It requires about 37 gallons of water, 1.3 KW hours of electricity, and about 1.5 lbs of wood to make one roll of toilet paper. Americans use about 34 million rolls of toilet paper every day. It takes 10-20 years for a tree to mature enough to harvest for toilet paper. In contrast, the plant-based biofilm we use for MaskIT is made with potatoes that have an 80-day growth cycle, making MaskIT Tampon Disposal Bags much more sustainable.
The bottom line is that toilet paper requires an unreasonable amount of resources to produce.

The sounds of the ocean’s waves around you; the mountain’s fresh aromas and clean air. You feel vibrant, alive, rested. So what are Anions?

There are two types of ions – positive and negative. Positive ions are atoms that have lost one or more electrons due to a high energy impact. Natural forces that generate positive ions include the decay of radioactive minerals, radon gas, forest fires, lightning and ultraviolet rays. Anions (or negative ions) are atoms or molecules having more electrons than protons and giving off what is known as a negative charge. In nature, negative ions are created with air molecules broken apart from sunlight, radiation, and moving air or water. Negative ions can be found in forests, near the ocean, and surrounding waterfalls. They have also been known to help relieve stress, alleviate depression and boost energy. Positive ions are considered harmful to the human body, while negative ions are considered beneficial.

LBL stands for Light Bladder Leakage, and it affects millions of women. In fact, 1 in 3 women experience Light Bladder Leakage (LBL). LBL is the frequent involuntary leakage of urine. Why do I have bladder leaks? Some of the most common reasons for uninvited leaks include: • Physical changes from childbirth to menopause. • Being overweight. • Complications from surgery, stroke, or chronic diseases. • Bladder or urinary tract infections. • Bladder irritants. Can I prevent leaks? description:
These are so comfortable, unlike regular pads. They are soft and WAY more absorbent than I thought they would be. In fact, I think they are MORE absorbent than normal disposable pads. Normal pads roll up sometimes, they can actually sound crunchy like a diaper, they don't breathe and are hot and sweaty, and they can smell disgusting. These are the opposite! They stay put despite not sticking to your underwear. They actually breathe and there is no "period smell" at all! I am so happy I found these but also so disappointed I never thought to try them years ago!

The medium fit great and are absorbent enough for even a very heavy flow. I went ahead and bought the large, though, so I could have enough to last through my cycle and for the added security for heavy flow overnight.

The washing instructions are to rinse the pad out after use and then just throw them in the wash on gentle. I experimented to make sure they wouldn't dye anything by doing a load with just the pads and a white hand towel and the white towel came out perfectly fine so I think it'll be fine to throw them in with other clothes. I air dried them because, even though the instructions say you can dry on low, I didn't want to risk the nice soft fabric pilling up.

All in all, I strongly recommend these!

UPDATE: I washed on gentle cycle and actually noticed a smell the next time I used them. The next time, I washed them on normal cycle with other laundry because they seemed very well made and sturdy. This worked and no smell. I think that the agitation of other clothes really helps get them clean. I still air-dried.

Frequently Asked Questions

What’s the difference between Always Ultra Thin and Always Maxi?
Always Ultra Thin pads, in the green package, are super-thin and highly absorbent. Always Maxis, in the blue package, provide the extra feeling of security many women get from using a thicker pad.

How do I put on a pad?
Always pads have adhesive strips to attach securely to your panties. Remove the paper backing and press the sticky side of the pad to your underwear. If your pad also has wings (extra flaps that fold over the sides of your underwear for increased protection), remove the paper backing and wrap the wings around the crotch, pressing firmly to the underside of your panties.

When should I change my pad?
You’ll want to change your pad regularly to stay clean and comfortable; usually every 3–4 hours or more often if your flow is heavy. Remember to match the absorbency of the pad (Regular, Super, or Overnight) to your flow, not your body type.

What’s in the pad?
Always pads have an absorbent core made of processed wood pulp between the plastic top and bottom layers. Always Ultra includes absorbent gelling material in the center of the pad. We use adhesive to hold the pad together.

Is there latex in the pads?
None of our currently marketed Always pads, pantiliners, wipes, or Quickwraps contain any natural rubber latex components. All ingredients in Always are extensively tested for safe use.

Frequently Asked Questions

What’s the difference between Always Ultra Thin and Always Maxi?
Always Ultra Thin pads, in the green package, are super-thin and highly absorbent. Always Maxis, in the blue package, provide the extra feeling of security many women get from using a thicker pad.

How do I put on a pad?
Always pads have adhesive strips to attach securely to your panties. Remove the paper backing and press the sticky side of the pad to your underwear. If your pad also has wings (extra flaps that fold over the sides of your underwear for increased protection), remove the paper backing and wrap the wings around the crotch, pressing firmly to the underside of your panties.

When should I change my pad?
You’ll want to change your pad regularly to stay clean and comfortable; usually every 3–4 hours or more often if your flow is heavy. Remember to match the absorbency of the pad (Regular, Super, or Overnight) to your flow, not your body type.

What’s in the pad?
Always pads have an absorbent core made of processed wood pulp between the plastic top and bottom layers. Always Ultra includes absorbent gelling material in the center of the pad. We use adhesive to hold the pad together.

Is there latex in the pads?
None of our currently marketed Always pads, pantiliners, wipes, or Quickwraps contain any natural rubber latex components. All ingredients in Always are extensively tested for safe use.

Patented Anion Strip Have you ever gone to the ocean or mountains and felt better because of the surroundings?

The sounds of the ocean’s waves around you; the mountain’s fresh aromas and clean air. You feel vibrant, alive, rested. So what are Anions?

There are two types of ions – positive and negative. Positive ions are atoms that have lost one or more electrons due to a high energy impact. Natural forces that generate positive ions include the decay of radioactive minerals, radon gas, forest fires, lightning and ultraviolet rays. Anions (or negative ions) are atoms or molecules having more electrons than protons and giving off what is known as a negative charge. In nature, negative ions are created with air molecules broken apart from sunlight, radiation, and moving air or water. Negative ions can be found in forests, near the ocean, and surrounding waterfalls. They have also been known to help relieve stress, alleviate depression and boost energy. Positive ions are considered harmful to the human body, while negative ions are considered beneficial.

¿Por qué algodón? ¿Por qué orgánico? El algodón transpirable permite un equilibrio natural de humedad, lo que significa que la piel respira y permanece hidratada. El algodón naturalmente suave y absorbente es naturalmente la fibra más suave y absorbente disponible y también es compatible con la piel. Suave con los materiales sintéticos de la piel y los polímeros súper absorbentes (savia) pueden causar irritación y sobrecalentamiento a la piel sensible. Mejor para su cuerpo el algodón orgánico se cultiva sin el uso de pesticidas persistentes que ayudan a proteger su cuerpo y limita los productos químicos tóxicos y duraderos en nuestro medio ambiente. Mejor para nuestro planeta la elección de comprar algodón orgánico es importante. El algodón cultivado orgánicamente tiene menos impacto ambiental que el algodón convencional, pero cuesta más producir, por lo que su decisión es una inversión directa en el futuro de nuestro planeta.

Warum Baumwolle? Warum Bio? Atmungsaktive Baumwolle ermöglicht ein natürliches Gleichgewicht von Feuchtigkeit, was bedeutet, dass die Haut atmet und hydratisiert bleibt. Natürlich weiche und saugfähige Baumwolle ist von Natur aus die weichste, saugfähigste Faser auf dem Markt und ist auch pH-kompatibel mit der Haut. Sanft zu Ihrer Haut, synthetische Materialien und super absorbierende Polymere (Sap) können Reizungen und Überhitzung auf empfindlicher Haut verursachen. Besser für Ihren Körper, Bio-Baumwolle wird ohne die Verwendung von dauerhaften Pestiziden angebaut, die Ihren Körper schützen und giftige und langlebige Chemikalien in unserer Umwelt begrenzen. Besser für unseren Planeten ist die Wahl, Bio-Baumwolle zu kaufen. Baumwolle aus biologischem Anbau hat weniger Umweltbelastung als herkömmliche Baumwolle, aber es kostet mehr zu produzieren, so dass Ihre Entscheidung eine direkte Investition in die Zukunft unseres Planeten ist.

למה כותנה? למה אורגני? כותנה נושמת מאפשרת איזון טבעי של לחות, מה שאומר שהעור נושם ונשאר רווי. כותנה רכה וסופגת באופן טבעי היא הסיבים הרכים והסופגים ביותר הקיימים והיא גם תואמת ph לעור. עדין על העור שלך חומרים סינתטיים ופולימרים סופגים במיוחד (סאפ) יכולים לגרום לגירוי והתחממות יתר לעור רגיש. טוב יותר עבור הגוף שלך כותנה אורגנית גדלה ללא שימוש בחומרי הדברה מתמשכים אשר מסייעים להגן על הגוף שלך ומגביל כימיקלים רעילים וארוכי טווח בסביבה שלנו. עדיף עבור כדור הארץ שלנו, הבחירה לרכוש כותנה אורגנית היא דבר חשוב. לכותנה אורגנית יש השפעה סביבתית נמוכה יותר מאשר כותנה קונבנציונלית אבל זה עולה יותר לייצר, אז ההחלטה שלך היא השקעה ישירה בעתיד של כדור הארץ.

Por que algodão? Por que orgânico? O algodão respirável permite um equilíbrio natural de umidade, o que significa que a pele respira e permanece hidratada. O algodão naturalmente macio e absorvente é naturalmente a fibra mais macia e absorvente disponível e também é compatível com pH com a pele. Materiais sintéticos suaves na sua pele e polímeros superabsorventes (seiva) podem causar irritação e superaquecimento para a pele sensível. Melhor para o seu corpo, o algodão orgânico é cultivado sem o uso de pesticidas persistentes, o que ajuda a proteger o seu corpo e limita produtos químicos tóxicos e de longa duração em nosso ambiente. Melhor para o nosso planeta, a escolha de comprar algodão orgânico é importante. O algodão orgânico tem menos impacto ambiental do que o algodão convencional, mas custa mais a produção, então sua decisão é um investimento direto no futuro do nosso planeta.

The sounds of the ocean’s waves around you; the mountain’s fresh aromas and clean air. You feel vibrant, alive, rested. So what are Anions?

There are two types of ions – positive and negative. Positive ions are atoms that have lost one or more electrons due to a high energy impact. Natural forces that generate positive ions include the decay of radioactive minerals, radon gas, forest fires, lightning and ultraviolet rays. Anions (or negative ions) are atoms or molecules having more electrons than protons and giving off what is known as a negative charge. In nature, negative ions are created with air molecules broken apart from sunlight, radiation, and moving air or water. Negative ions can be found in forests, near the ocean, and surrounding waterfalls. They have also been known to help relieve stress, alleviate depression and boost energy. Positive ions are considered harmful to the human body, while negative ions are considered beneficial.

Patented Anion Strip Have you ever gone to the ocean or mountains and felt better because of the surroundings?

The sounds of the ocean’s waves around you; the mountain’s fresh aromas and clean air. You feel vibrant, alive, rested. So what are Anions?

There are two types of ions – positive and negative. Positive ions are atoms that have lost one or more electrons due to a high energy impact. Natural forces that generate positive ions include the decay of radioactive minerals, radon gas, forest fires, lightning and ultraviolet rays. Anions (or negative ions) are atoms or molecules having more electrons than protons and giving off what is known as a negative charge. In nature, negative ions are created with air molecules broken apart from sunlight, radiation, and moving air or water. Negative ions can be found in forests, near the ocean, and surrounding waterfalls. They have also been known to help relieve stress, alleviate depression and boost energy. Positive ions are considered harmful to the human body, while negative ions are considered beneficial.

You feel vibrant, alive, rested. So what are Anions? There are two types of ions - positive and negative. Positive ions are atoms that have lost one or more electrons due to a high energy impact. Natural forces that generate positive ions include the decay of radioactive minerals, radon gas, forest fires, lightning and ultraviolet rays. Anions (or negative ions) are atoms or molecules having more electrons than protons and giving off what is known as a negative charge. In nature, negative ions are created with air molecules broken apart from sunlight, radiation, and moving air or water. description: hannah is a brand that always thinks about ways to help women experience more comfortable and enjoyable menstrual cycles. It’s already been over 16 years since hannah was first launched back in 2005; it was born with hopes to alleviate pain and decrease side effects for women using disposable pads. Even with many challenges along the way, hannah was able to grow and expand thanks to all of our valued customers and their feedbacks over the years. It only began as a small night time job with just a few fabrics and a sewing machine. From a one person dream, hannah is now a company with professional seamstresses and management team, where everyone works together to make exceptional quality cloth pads and also finds ways to give back to the society. It was difficult (and still is) to change people’s minds about menstruation. It is not a ‘taboo’ nor a ‘disgusting thing’. Many people think cloth pads are smelly and filthy because of the blood, and so nobody wants to touch it. However, it’s not your period blood that stinks. The odor occurs due to the chemical reaction and bacterial growth from the blood touching the disposable pads. We will face these questions as we go forward with our products. Of course you cannot overlook the convenience of disposable pads. Nevertheless, the plastic and chemicals in disposable pads harm the environment and it is our goal to minimize this with hannah. We are always looking for ways to make hannah achieve the next level. Designed in Korea and manufactured in Korea and Vietnam, all of our products are creations and developments from real user experiences and feedbacks. We do love to hear from you on how hannah can become better. After all, it’s all about you.

Frequently Asked Questions

What’s the difference between Always Ultra Thin and Always Maxi?
Always Ultra Thin pads, in the green package, are super-thin and highly absorbent. Always Maxis, in the blue package, provide the extra feeling of security many women get from using a thicker pad.

How do I put on a pad?
Always pads have adhesive strips to attach securely to your panties. Remove the paper backing and press the sticky side of the pad to your underwear. If your pad also has wings (extra flaps that fold over the sides of your underwear for increased protection), remove the paper backing and wrap the wings around the crotch, pressing firmly to the underside of your panties.

When should I change my pad?
You’ll want to change your pad regularly to stay clean and comfortable; usually every 3–4 hours or more often if your flow is heavy. Remember to match the absorbency of the pad (Regular, Super, or Overnight) to your flow, not your body type.

What’s in the pad?
Always pads have an absorbent core made of processed wood pulp between the plastic top and bottom layers. Always Ultra includes absorbent gelling material in the center of the pad. We use adhesive to hold the pad together.

Is there latex in the pads?
None of our currently marketed Always pads, pantiliners, wipes, or Quickwraps contain any natural rubber latex components. All ingredients in Always are extensively tested for safe use.

Pads can be easily washed by hand or machine in any temperature with your regular detergent. Pre-soaking or rinsing in cold water prior to washing is recommended (but not always necessary) if your pad is heavily saturated. Do not soak for longer than 24 hours.

description:
A Better Way To Manage Your Period
On average, a woman will experience 30 or so years of menstruation in her lifetime, from her first period to menopause. Just one year's supply of disposable pads and tampons can cost between $60 and $120. Doing the math (and lowballing it), that's around $3,600 in a lifetime on a NECCESITY. In addition to that, tampons, panty liners and sanitary napkins, along with their applicator and packaging contribute to around 200,000 tonnes of waste per year. Enter Reusable Menstrual Pads, an alternative that is equally as effective as sanitary pads and tampons.

Why The Hive's Reusable Sanitary Pad?
Our washable pads are free from harmful substances, they are skin friendly, comfortable, sustainable and economical!

What Are The Sizes Available?

  • Liner- 19cm/7.5 inches
  • Regular- 21cm/8.3 inches
  • Ultra- 24cm/9.5 inches

How Do I Clean The Pads?
We suggest rinsing the pads thoroughly under running water, then place them in the washing machine, best to use eco-friendly detergent, cold or warm wash recommended. Best to air dry. If using the dryer, LOW TEMPERATURE setting recommended.
Note: Do not use fabric softener or bleach.

How Often Do I Need To Change The Pads?
Naturally, if your flow is heavy, you will have to change pads more frequently. If your flow is lighter, the longer you can take between changes.

How Do I Deal With Pad Changes When I'm On The Go?
You can fold them up into perfect little squares that you can pack away in your purse. You probably will want to carry a waterproof bag with you to keep the used pads, you can wash them at home.

What Is The Shelf Life of The Hive's Sanitary Pad?
Depending on how well you take care of it, the pads can be used for the next 10 years!

description:
These are so comfortable, unlike regular pads. They are soft and WAY more absorbent than I thought they would be. In fact, I think they are MORE absorbent than normal disposable pads. Normal pads roll up sometimes, they can actually sound crunchy like a diaper, they don't breathe and are hot and sweaty, and they can smell disgusting. These are the opposite! They stay put despite not sticking to your underwear. They actually breathe and there is no "period smell" at all! I am so happy I found these but also so disappointed I never thought to try them years ago!

The medium fit great and are absorbent enough for even a very heavy flow. I went ahead and bought the large, though, so I could have enough to last through my cycle and for the added security for heavy flow overnight.

The washing instructions are to rinse the pad out after use and then just throw them in the wash on gentle. I experimented to make sure they wouldn't dye anything by doing a load with just the pads and a white hand towel and the white towel came out perfectly fine so I think it'll be fine to throw them in with other clothes. I air dried them because, even though the instructions say you can dry on low, I didn't want to risk the nice soft fabric pilling up.

All in all, I strongly recommend these!

UPDATE: I washed on gentle cycle and actually noticed a smell the next time I used them. The next time, I washed them on normal cycle with other laundry because they seemed very well made and sturdy. This worked and no smell. I think that the agitation of other clothes really helps get them clean. I still air-dried.

Frequently Asked Questions

What’s the difference between Always Ultra Thin and Always Maxi?
Always Ultra Thin pads, in the green package, are super-thin and highly absorbent. Always Maxis, in the blue package, provide the extra feeling of security many women get from using a thicker pad.

How do I put on a pad?
Always pads have adhesive strips to attach securely to your panties. Remove the paper backing and press the sticky side of the pad to your underwear. If your pad also has wings (extra flaps that fold over the sides of your underwear for increased protection), remove the paper backing and wrap the wings around the crotch, pressing firmly to the underside of your panties.

When should I change my pad?
You’ll want to change your pad regularly to stay clean and comfortable; usually every 3–4 hours or more often if your flow is heavy. Remember to match the absorbency of the pad (Regular, Super, or Overnight) to your flow, not your body type.

What’s in the pad?
Always pads have an absorbent core made of processed wood pulp between the plastic top and bottom layers. Always Ultra includes absorbent gelling material in the center of the pad. We use adhesive to hold the pad together.

Is there latex in the pads?
None of our currently marketed Always pads, pantiliners, wipes, or Quickwraps contain any natural rubber latex components. All ingredients in Always are extensively tested for safe use.

Frequently Asked Questions

What’s the difference between Always Ultra Thin and Always Maxi?
Always Ultra Thin pads, in the green package, are super-thin and highly absorbent. Always Maxis, in the blue package, provide the extra feeling of security many women get from using a thicker pad.

How do I put on a pad?
Always pads have adhesive strips to attach securely to your panties. Remove the paper backing and press the sticky side of the pad to your underwear. If your pad also has wings (extra flaps that fold over the sides of your underwear for increased protection), remove the paper backing and wrap the wings around the crotch, pressing firmly to the underside of your panties.

When should I change my pad?
You’ll want to change your pad regularly to stay clean and comfortable; usually every 3–4 hours or more often if your flow is heavy. Remember to match the absorbency of the pad (Regular, Super, or Overnight) to your flow, not your body type.

What’s in the pad?
Always pads have an absorbent core made of processed wood pulp between the plastic top and bottom layers. Always Ultra includes absorbent gelling material in the center of the pad. We use adhesive to hold the pad together.

Is there latex in the pads?
None of our currently marketed Always pads, pantiliners, wipes, or Quickwraps contain any natural rubber latex components. All ingredients in Always are extensively tested for safe use.

Patented Anion Strip Have you ever gone to the ocean or mountains and felt better because of the surroundings?

The sounds of the ocean’s waves around you; the mountain’s fresh aromas and clean air. You feel vibrant, alive, rested. So what are Anions?

There are two types of ions – positive and negative. Positive ions are atoms that have lost one or more electrons due to a high energy impact. Natural forces that generate positive ions include the decay of radioactive minerals, radon gas, forest fires, lightning and ultraviolet rays. Anions (or negative ions) are atoms or molecules having more electrons than protons and giving off what is known as a negative charge. In nature, negative ions are created with air molecules broken apart from sunlight, radiation, and moving air or water. Negative ions can be found in forests, near the ocean, and surrounding waterfalls. They have also been known to help relieve stress, alleviate depression and boost energy. description:
About Us:
At the core of who we are is the desire to do good, be good and spread good to people, communities, and the environment; Our company was founded on these values and they still guide us today. It is through conscious intention that we offer the cleanest disposal method available, in the cleanest way possible. Our commitment to excellence makes MaskIT tampon disposal bags the premier choice for anyone who wants the best.
MaskIT Sustainability:
We love our planet and do everything we can to reduce our ecological footprint. MaskIT disposal bags are made with plant-based biofilm, derived from the starches of plants and vegetables (mostly potatoes). Our potato-based biofilm does NOT contain any polyethylene or plastic materials whatsoever. In fact, our biofilm can be consumed by microorganisms that naturally live in our soil. Our packaging is made with 100% post-consumer paper and is printed with soy-based ink in a facility that operates on 100% renewable energy.
Why not just use toilet paper?
It requires about 37 gallons of water, 1.3 KW hours of electricity, and about 1.5 lbs of wood to make one roll of toilet paper. Americans use about 34 million rolls of toilet paper every day. It takes 10-20 years for a tree to mature enough to harvest for toilet paper. In contrast, the plant-based biofilm we use for MaskIT is made with potatoes that have an 80-day growth cycle, making MaskIT Tampon Disposal Bags much more sustainable.
The bottom line is that toilet paper requires an unreasonable amount of resources to produce.

description:
These are so comfortable, unlike regular pads. They are soft and WAY more absorbent than I thought they would be. In fact, I think they are MORE absorbent than normal disposable pads. Normal pads roll up sometimes, they can actually sound crunchy like a diaper, they don't breathe and are hot and sweaty, and they can smell disgusting. These are the opposite! They stay put despite not sticking to your underwear. They actually breathe and there is no "period smell" at all! I am so happy I found these but also so disappointed I never thought to try them years ago!

The medium fit great and are absorbent enough for even a very heavy flow. I went ahead and bought the large, though, so I could have enough to last through my cycle and for the added security for heavy flow overnight.

The washing instructions are to rinse the pad out after use and then just throw them in the wash on gentle. I experimented to make sure they wouldn't dye anything by doing a load with just the pads and a white hand towel and the white towel came out perfectly fine so I think it'll be fine to throw them in with other clothes. I air dried them because, even though the instructions say you can dry on low, I didn't want to risk the nice soft fabric pilling up.

All in all, I strongly recommend these!

UPDATE: I washed on gentle cycle and actually noticed a smell the next time I used them. The next time, I washed them on normal cycle with other laundry because they seemed very well made and sturdy. This worked and no smell. I think that the agitation of other clothes really helps get them clean. I still air-dried.

description:
About Us:
At the core of who we are is the desire to do good, be good and spread good to people, communities, and the environment; Our company was founded on these values and they still guide us today. It is through conscious intention that we offer the cleanest disposal method available, in the cleanest way possible. Our commitment to excellence makes MaskIT tampon disposal bags the premier choice for anyone who wants the best.
MaskIT Sustainability:
We love our planet and do everything we can to reduce our ecological footprint. MaskIT disposal bags are made with plant-based biofilm, derived from the starches of plants and vegetables (mostly potatoes). Our potato-based biofilm does NOT contain any polyethylene or plastic materials whatsoever. In fact, our biofilm can be consumed by microorganisms that naturally live in our soil. Our packaging is made with 100% post-consumer paper and is printed with soy-based ink in a facility that operates on 100% renewable energy.
Why not just use toilet paper?
It requires about 37 gallons of water, 1.3 KW hours of electricity, and about 1.5 lbs of wood to make one roll of toilet paper. Americans use about 34 million rolls of toilet paper every day. It takes 10-20 years for a tree to mature enough to harvest for toilet paper. In contrast, the plant-based biofilm we use for MaskIT is made with potatoes that have an 80-day growth cycle, making MaskIT Tampon Disposal Bags much more sustainable.
The bottom line is that toilet paper requires an unreasonable amount of resources to produce.

description: SochGreen Interlabial pads are much smaller than panty liners and are to be worn externally along with cloth pads or menstrual cup. The petal pad is a small, petal shaped, pad that is tucked between the labia (lips or folds of skin at the vaginal opening) to catch the menstrual flow much closer to the vagina to avoid messy leaks during heavy flow/ flow with clots. The pad has no leakproof backing, and will leak as they fill up, so be aware that these are only used for very light absorbency - more like a liner than a pad. You can place it as it is or fold in half or roll it up to form a cylinder and place between the labia. This will help regulate your flow towards the centre of your pad. This is useful for those who tend to have more front, back or side - bleeding patterns. Using these, along with cloth pads will significantly increase the time you can wear your cloth pads. As these are held in place by the labia, you need to be careful while going to the loo, and make sure you do not drop them in the toilet seat. You must remove the labia pad before sitting on the toilet. You can also stitch these on top of your existing cloth pads to increase their absorbency. Or use them as a back-up to your menstrual cup. Back of each pad has a small loop to accommodate a string provided. These are to help you in washing, drying and storing your Interlabia pads so they do not get lost in your washing machine / drying line. DO's:-Always use a clean and dry pad. Use mild soap to clean the pad; rinse thoroughly to make sure no soap remains on the pad. Dry it in direct sunlight when possible, or dry in your machine on low heat. Store in clean and dry place. Wash the Interlabial pad before first use. DONT's:-Do not soak/wash the pad in hot water as it will set stains. Never use a wet/damp pad. Do not store a wet/damp pad in your cupboard. Do not brush the Interlabial pad.

description:
These are so comfortable, unlike regular pads. They are soft and WAY more absorbent than I thought they would be. In fact, I think they are MORE absorbent than normal disposable pads. Normal pads roll up sometimes, they can actually sound crunchy like a diaper, they don't breathe and are hot and sweaty, and they can smell disgusting. These are the opposite! They stay put despite not sticking to your underwear. They actually breathe and there is no "period smell" at all! I am so happy I found these but also so disappointed I never thought to try them years ago!

The medium fit great and are absorbent enough for even a very heavy flow. I went ahead and bought the large, though, so I could have enough to last through my cycle and for the added security for heavy flow overnight.

The washing instructions are to rinse the pad out after use and then just throw them in the wash on gentle. I experimented to make sure they wouldn't dye anything by doing a load with just the pads and a white hand towel and the white towel came out perfectly fine so I think it'll be fine to throw them in with other clothes. I air dried them because, even though the instructions say you can dry on low, I didn't want to risk the nice soft fabric pilling up.

All in all, I strongly recommend these!

UPDATE: I washed on gentle cycle and actually noticed a smell the next time I used them. The next time, I washed them on normal cycle with other laundry because they seemed very well made and sturdy. This worked and no smell. I think that the agitation of other clothes really helps get them clean. I still air-dried.

¿Por qué algodón? ¿Por qué orgánico? El algodón transpirable permite un equilibrio natural de humedad, lo que significa que la piel respira y permanece hidratada. El algodón naturalmente suave y absorbente es naturalmente la fibra más suave y absorbente disponible y también es compatible con la piel. Suave con los materiales sintéticos de la piel y los polímeros súper absorbentes (savia) pueden causar irritación y sobrecalentamiento a la piel sensible. Mejor para su cuerpo el algodón orgánico se cultiva sin el uso de pesticidas persistentes que ayudan a proteger su cuerpo y limita los productos químicos tóxicos y duraderos en nuestro medio ambiente. Mejor para nuestro planeta la elección de comprar algodón orgánico es importante. El algodón cultivado orgánicamente tiene menos impacto ambiental que el algodón convencional, pero cuesta más producir, por lo que su decisión es una inversión directa en el futuro de nuestro planeta.

Warum Baumwolle? Warum Bio? Atmungsaktive Baumwolle ermöglicht ein natürliches Gleichgewicht von Feuchtigkeit, was bedeutet, dass die Haut atmet und hydratisiert bleibt. Natürlich weiche und saugfähige Baumwolle ist von Natur aus die weichste, saugfähigste Faser auf dem Markt und ist auch pH-kompatibel mit der Haut. Sanft zu Ihrer Haut, synthetische Materialien und super absorbierende Polymere (Sap) können Reizungen und Überhitzung auf empfindlicher Haut verursachen. Besser für Ihren Körper, Bio-Baumwolle wird ohne die Verwendung von dauerhaften Pestiziden angebaut, die Ihren Körper schützen und giftige und langlebige Chemikalien in unserer Umwelt begrenzen. Besser für unseren Planeten ist die Wahl, Bio-Baumwolle zu kaufen. Baumwolle aus biologischem Anbau hat weniger Umweltbelastung als herkömmliche Baumwolle, aber es kostet mehr zu produzieren, so dass Ihre Entscheidung eine direkte Investition in die Zukunft unseres Planeten ist.

למה כותנה? למה אורגני? כותנה נושמת מאפשרת איזון טבעי של לחות, מה שאומר שהעור נושם ונשאר רווי. כותנה רכה וסופגת באופן טבעי היא הסיבים הרכים והסופגים ביותר הקיימים והיא גם תואמת ph לעור. עדין על העור שלך חומרים סינתטיים ופולימרים סופגים במיוחד (סאפ) יכולים לגרום לגירוי והתחממות יתר לעור רגיש. טוב יותר עבור הגוף שלך כותנה אורגנית גדלה ללא שימוש בחומרי הדברה מתמשכים אשר מסייעים להגן על הגוף שלך ומגביל כימיקלים רעילים וארוכי טווח בסביבה שלנו. עדיף עבור כדור הארץ שלנו, הבחירה לרכוש כותנה אורגנית היא דבר חשוב. לכותנה אורגנית יש השפעה סביבתית נמוכה יותר מאשר כותנה קונבנציונלית אבל זה עולה יותר לייצר, אז ההחלטה שלך היא השקעה ישירה בעתיד של כדור הארץ.

Por que algodão? Por que orgânico? O algodão respirável permite um equilíbrio natural de umidade, o que significa que a pele respira e permanece hidratada. O algodão naturalmente macio e absorvente é naturalmente a fibra mais macia e absorvente disponível e também é compatível com pH com a pele. Materiais sintéticos suaves na sua pele e polímeros superabsorventes (seiva) podem causar irritação e superaquecimento para a pele sensível. Melhor para o seu corpo, o algodão orgânico é cultivado sem o uso de pesticidas persistentes, o que ajuda a proteger o seu corpo e limita produtos químicos tóxicos e de longa duração em nosso ambiente. Melhor para o nosso planeta, a escolha de comprar algodão orgânico é importante. O algodão orgânico tem menos impacto ambiental do que o algodão convencional, mas custa mais a produção, então sua decisão é um investimento direto no futuro do nosso planeta.

为什么选择棉? 为什么选择有机? 透气棉质面料可实现自然的水分平衡,这意味着皮肤透气并保持水分。 天然柔软吸水棉是市面上最柔软、最吸水的纤维,也是 pH 值与皮肤兼容。 温和呵护您的皮肤合成材料和超强吸水性聚合物(汁液)可对敏感皮肤造成刺激和过热。 更好的适合您的身体,有机棉种植时不使用持久的农药,这有助于保护您的身体,并限制环境中的有毒和持久的化学物质。 购买有机棉是一个重要的选择。 有机种植的棉花比传统棉花对环境影响较小,但生产成本更高,因此您的决定是我们地球未来的直接投资。

為什麼要用棉? 為什麼要有機? 透氣的棉質可以平衡水分,這意味著皮膚可以呼吸並保持水分。 天然柔軟吸水棉天然是最柔軟、最吸水性的纖維,也與 PH 值皮膚相容。 對皮膚溫和合成材料和超吸水聚合物(sap)可能會對敏感肌膚造成刺激和過熱。 Better for your body (更好的身體),不使用持久的殺蟲劑,有助於保護您的身體,並限制我們環境中有毒和持久的化學物質。 對我們的星球來說,選擇購買有機棉是非常重要的。 有機種植棉對環境的影響比傳統棉花要小,但生產成本更高,因此您的決定是對我們地球未來的直接投資。

왜 면을 사용할까요? 왜 유기농일까요? 통기성이 좋은 면은 자연스러운 수분 균형을 제공하므로 피부가 숨을 쉬고 수분을 유지합니다. 자연적으로 부드럽고 흡수력이 좋은 면은 자연적으로 가장 부드럽고 흡수력이 좋은 섬유이며 피부와 호환됩니다. 피부에 부드러운 합성 소재와 흡수력이 뛰어난 폴리머 (수액)는 민감한 피부에 자극과 과열을 일으킬 수 있습니다. 몸에 더 좋은 유기농 면은 지속적인 살충제를 사용하지 않고 재배되어 몸을 보호하고 우리 환경에서 독성과 오래 지속되는 화학 물질을 제한합니다. 우리 지구에 더 좋은 유기농 면을 구매하는 것이 중요합니다. 유기농으로 재배 된 면은 기존 면보다 환경에 미치는 영향은 적지만 생산하는데 더 많은 비용이 들기 때문에 지구의 미래에 대한 직접적인 투자입니다.

LBL stands for Light Bladder Leakage, and it affects millions of women. In fact, 1 in 3 women experience Light Bladder Leakage (LBL). LBL is the frequent involuntary leakage of urine. Why do I have bladder leaks? Some of the most common reasons for uninvited leaks include: • Physical changes from childbirth to menopause. • Being overweight. • Complications from surgery, stroke, or chronic diseases. • Bladder or urinary tract infections. • Bladder irritants. Can I prevent leaks? There are healthy habits you can maintain in order to help prevent leaks. • Track your triggers – Look for patterns in how your bladder reacts to certain spicy and acidic foods and beverages. • Exercise regularly - Reduce leaks by strengthening the muscles of your pelvic floor. • Drink more water – Drink six to seven 8-ounce glasses of water a day to prevent irritation. These are so comfortable, unlike regular pads. They are soft and WAY more absorbent than I thought they would be. In fact, I think they are MORE absorbent than normal disposable pads. Normal pads roll up sometimes, they can actually sound crunchy like a diaper, they don't breathe and are hot and sweaty, and they can smell disgusting. These are the opposite! They stay put despite not sticking to your underwear. They actually breathe and there is no "period smell" at all! I am so happy I found these but also so disappointed I never thought to try them years ago!

The medium fit great and are absorbent enough for even a very heavy flow. I went ahead and bought the large, though, so I could have enough to last through my cycle and for the added security for heavy flow overnight.

The washing instructions are to rinse the pad out after use and then just throw them in the wash on gentle. I experimented to make sure they wouldn't dye anything by doing a load with just the pads and a white hand towel and the white towel came out perfectly fine so I think it'll be fine to throw them in with other clothes. I air dried them because, even though the instructions say you can dry on low, I didn't want to risk the nice soft fabric pilling up.

All in all, I strongly recommend these!

UPDATE: I washed on gentle cycle and actually noticed a smell the next time I used them. The next time, I washed them on normal cycle with other laundry because they seemed very well made and sturdy. This worked and no smell. I think that the agitation of other clothes really helps get them clean. I still air-dried.

Patented Anion Strip Have you ever gone to the ocean or mountains and felt better because of the surroundings?

The sounds of the ocean’s waves around you; the mountain’s fresh aromas and clean air. You feel vibrant, alive, rested. So what are Anions?

There are two types of ions – positive and negative. Positive ions are atoms that have lost one or more electrons due to a high energy impact. Natural forces that generate positive ions include the decay of radioactive minerals, radon gas, forest fires, lightning and ultraviolet rays. Anions (or negative ions) are atoms or molecules having more electrons than protons and giving off what is known as a negative charge. In nature, negative ions are created with air molecules broken apart from sunlight, radiation, and moving air or water. Negative ions can be found in forests, near the ocean, and surrounding waterfalls. They have also been known to help relieve stress, alleviate depression and boost energy. Positive ions are considered harmful to the human body, while negative ions are considered beneficial.

Healthy Essentials For Your Body And Our Environment

Maxim Hygiene offers healthy, sustainable hygiene products that are safe for your body and the environment.

What looks like Cotton in other products is not always 100% Cotton. Wood Pulp and Synthetics that may be bleached with Chlorine are often used as a substitute in conventional women’s hygiene products. All Maxim products are made with 100% Organic and Natural Chlorine-Free Cotton to help reduce the risk of irritation, minimize the body's exposure to chemicals and feel softer.

The perfect sanitary pad should provide maximum comfort and protection. That’s what these organic cotton pads with wings deliver. Maxim’s modern design with innovative leakage control channels allows you to go about your day with peace of mind knowing that you’re protected against leaks and accidents as well as treating your body with the finest natural materials. These organic winged pads provide enough protection to be used throughout the day.

Patented Anion Strip

Have you ever gone to the ocean or mountains and felt better because of the surroundings? The sounds of the ocean’s waves around you; the mountain’s fresh aromas and clean air. You feel vibrant, alive, rested.


So what are Anions?

There are two types of ions – positive and negative. Positive ions are atoms that have lost one or more electrons due to a high energy impact. Natural forces that generate positive ions include the decay of radioactive minerals, radon gas, forest fires, lightning and ultraviolet rays.

Anions (or negative ions) are atoms or molecules having more electrons than protons and giving off what is known as a negative charge. In nature, negative ions are created with air molecules broken apart from sunlight, radiation, and moving air or water. Negative ions can be found in forests, near the ocean, and surrounding waterfalls. They have also been known to help relieve stress, alleviate depression and boost energy.

description:
A Better Way To Manage Your Period
On average, a woman will experience 30 or so years of menstruation in her lifetime, from her first period to menopause. Just one year's supply of disposable pads and tampons can cost between $60 and $120. Doing the math (and lowballing it), that's around $3,600 in a lifetime on a NECCESITY. In addition to that, tampons, panty liners and sanitary napkins, along with their applicator and packaging contribute to around 200,000 tonnes of waste per year. Enter Reusable Menstrual Pads, an alternative that is equally as effective as sanitary pads and tampons.

Why The Hive's Reusable Sanitary Pad?
Our washable pads are free from harmful substances, they are skin friendly, comfortable, sustainable and economical!

What Are The Sizes Available?

  • Liner- 19cm/7.5 inches
  • Regular- 21cm/8.3 inches
  • Ultra- 24cm/9.5 inches

How Do I Clean The Pads?
We suggest rinsing the pads thoroughly under running water, then place them in the washing machine, best to use eco-friendly detergent, cold or warm wash recommended. Best to air dry. If using the dryer, LOW TEMPERATURE setting recommended.
Note: Do not use fabric softener or bleach.

How Often Do I Need To Change The Pads?
Naturally, if your flow is heavy, you will have to change pads more frequently. If your flow is lighter, the longer you can take between changes.

How Do I Deal With Pad Changes When I'm On The Go?
You can fold them up into perfect little squares that you can pack away in your purse. You probably will want to carry a waterproof bag with you to keep the used pads, you can wash them at home.

What Is The Shelf Life of The Hive's Sanitary Pad?
Depending on how well you take care of it, the pads can be used for the next 10 years!

description:
These are so comfortable, unlike regular pads. They are soft and WAY more absorbent than I thought they would be. In fact, I think they are MORE absorbent than normal disposable pads. Normal pads roll up sometimes, they can actually sound crunchy like a diaper, they don't breathe and are hot and sweaty, and they can smell disgusting. These are the opposite! They stay put despite not sticking to your underwear. They actually breathe and there is no "period smell" at all! I am so happy I found these but also so disappointed I never thought to try them years ago!

The medium fit great and are absorbent enough for even a very heavy flow. I went ahead and bought the large, though, so I could have enough to last through my cycle and for the added security for heavy flow overnight.

The washing instructions are to rinse the pad out after use and then just throw them in the wash on gentle. I experimented to make sure they wouldn't dye anything by doing a load with just the pads and a white hand towel and the white towel came out perfectly fine so I think it'll be fine to throw them in with other clothes. I air dried them because, even though the instructions say you can dry on low, I didn't want to risk the nice soft fabric pilling up.

All in all, I strongly recommend these!

UPDATE: I washed on gentle cycle and actually noticed a smell the next time I used them. The next time, I washed them on normal cycle with other laundry because they seemed very well made and sturdy. This worked and no smell. I think that the agitation of other clothes really helps get them clean. I still air-dried.

description:
The CDC indicates that each year roughly 48 million people, 1 in 6 Americans, get sick by consuming contaminated foods or beverages. Plenty kitchen care pads are designed to help protect you and your family from foodborne illnesses by absorbing the juices from raw meats, not allowing them to cross contaminate your counters or other foods. When preparing food, simply place a small or medium cutting board on top of the kitchen care pad and any juices that roll off the cutting board will be absorbed by the pad and protect your counters and your family. Each durable and disposable pad measures 17 inches wide by 24 inches long and provides a large surface area of kitchen counter protection while you work. These can also be used without a cutting board to place food on while keeping your food and counters clean and protected. When finished, simply place the pad in the garbage; no need to clean and sanitize your counter, thanks to the minimal mess you've created. Plenty kitchen care pads can also be used as a drying mat for fruits, vegetables, and kitchen utensils. They are also great for lots of non-kitchen activities, including gardening, arts and crafts, picnics, camping, hunting, as a floor mat for muddy shoes or other messy activities such as changing your car oil. Plenty kitchen care pads are manufactured in Pennsylvania with attention to quality, safety, sustainability and responsible sourcing practices by First Quality, a family-owned company. First Quality is a leader in developing premium quality products at a great value.

Frequently Asked Questions
Are Plenty kitchen care pads safe for direct food contact?
Yes, all materials used are considered safe for direct food contact by the FDA.

What materials are in Plenty kitchen care pads?
The top layer, which contacts the food, is made from 100% polypropylene. The bottom layer is made from a blend of polyethylene and polypropylene. The absorbent core is made from cellulose which is a natural material that is derived from trees.

Will Plenty kitchen care pads alter the taste, smell, or consistency of my food?
Not at all. These pads have been designed to only absorb the free flowing liquid for the food that they come in contact with and not transfer anything to the food.

How do I know how many Plenty kitchen care pads to use to prepare food?
For families of 3-6 people, usually one is enough, but it will depend upon how much free flowing liquid comes from your food. If you find that the kitchen care pad isn’t able to absorb all the free flowing liquid, you may need to use two. If you are using an extra-large cutting board you may want to use two.

Do Plenty kitchen care pads kill bacteria?
No they do not, but by absorbing the free flowing liquid of foods, it helps to reduce the potential to cross contaminate to other foods, surfaces and utensils.

Is this item durable?
Plenty kitchen care pads are mainly meant for the quick convenient protection of surfaces by absorbing liquids and collecting debris. You cannot cut meat directly on it.

Are Plenty kitchen care pads sterilized?
No they are not. They are made under the FDA’s CGMP (Current Good Manufacturing Process) requirements for sanitary products.

Is this item easy to use?
Plenty kitchen care pads are ready-to-use in seconds. Just unfold when removing from the package and place it on you work surface. Also, once done just fold the pad up to contain any liquid or debris and throw in the trash.

What are the dimensions of this item?
The Plenty kitchen care pad is 17 by 24 inches and easily accommodates small and medium sized cutting boards.

description:
About Us:
At the core of who we are is the desire to do good, be good and spread good to people, communities, and the environment; Our company was founded on these values and they still guide us today. It is through conscious intention that we offer the cleanest disposal method available, in the cleanest way possible. Our commitment to excellence makes MaskIT tampon disposal bags the premier choice for anyone who wants the best.
MaskIT Sustainability:
We love our planet and do everything we can to reduce our ecological footprint. MaskIT disposal bags are made with plant-based biofilm, derived from the starches of plants and vegetables (mostly potatoes). Our potato-based biofilm does NOT contain any polyethylene or plastic materials whatsoever. In fact, our biofilm can be consumed by microorganisms that naturally live in our soil. Our packaging is made with 100% post-consumer paper and is printed with soy-based ink in a facility that operates on 100% renewable energy.
Why not just use toilet paper?
It requires about 37 gallons of water, 1.3 KW hours of electricity, and about 1.5 lbs of wood to make one roll of toilet paper. Americans use about 34 million rolls of toilet paper every day. It takes 10-20 years for a tree to mature enough to harvest for toilet paper. In contrast, the plant-based biofilm we use for MaskIT is made with potatoes that have an 80-day growth cycle, making MaskIT Tampon Disposal Bags much more sustainable.
The bottom line is that toilet paper requires an unreasonable amount of resources to produce.
